reasoning:
Both cables are failing simultaneously: cable 1 symmetric (both /SENSEC1_HI and /SENSEC1_LO in failing_reasons, counted in kelvin_unrouted=1) and cable 2 asymmetric (/SENSEC2_HI only, NOT in kelvin_unrouted). The scorer penalizes cable 1 via kelvin_unrouted (1000) + 2x unconnected (2000) + gate_fail (1000); cable 2's asymmetric failure is penalized only via unconnected (1000) and the already-triggered gate_fail (0 marginal cost since gate_fail is binary and cable 1 already tripped it). This asymmetry means a candidate that clears cable 1 fully but leaves cable 2 asymmetrically failing scores identically on gate_fail as one that fails both, creating a false scoring equivalence.

The co-occurrence pattern is diagnostic: Rule 59's rationale identified cable 2's /SENSEC2_HI as newly failing starting around round 110, timed with Rule 58's post-max-escalation corridor ripup for cable 1. Rule 59 correctly protects cable 2's existing Kelvin track segments from being ripped during Rule 58's corridor clearance. However, Rule 59 does NOT prevent the newly-rerouted traffic (displaced from cable 1's freshly-cleared corridor) from being placed in cable 2's shunt tap window in the SAME round R+1. The competitor tracks re-entrench in cable 2's corridor before Rule 56/60's independent threshold fires for cable 2 (cable 2's consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[2] is ~3 after rounds 110-112, still 3 rounds short of the threshold-6 trigger). The three-round lag is the structural gap: Rule 58 creates a routing void that FR immediately fills, and some of that fill lands in the only adjacent open corridor space -- cable 2's tap window.

All 7 compiler stubs again fully eliminated (absorbed 3 + orphans 2 + spurs 2). No directed guidance reached FR. The three signal nets /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA were absorbed (those nets are already routed and the stubs were redundant false-positives), so the active unconnected ratlines are attributable to the Kelvin nets rather than signal net stub elimination. The proposed scorer penalty targets the scoring asymmetry between symmetric and asymmetric Kelvin failures. The proposed manager rule closes the one-round entrenchment window after Rule 58 ripup.

scorer_penalty.rationale: gate_fail is binary (0 or 1) and currently contributes 1000 regardless of whether one or two cables are failing. With cable 2's asymmetric failure providing zero MARGINAL penalty on gate_fail (it is already 1 from cable 1), the scorer cannot distinguish a candidate that clears cable 1 fully but leaves cable 2 asymmetrically failing from one that fails both. Raising gate_fail to 2000 doubles the binary gate-failure cost, widening the gap between gate-failing and gate-passing candidates in objective space. At the current drc=43 (200/violation = 8600 contribution), the gate_fail contribution of 1000 is small relative to DRC mass; raising to 2000 restores the intended dominance of hard-gate failures over DRC accumulation when selecting among multi-seed candidates.

manager_rule: When Rule 58 fires for cable C in round R (post-max-escalation corridor ripup: post_max_escalation_stall[C] reaches 4), AND in that same round R any OTHER cable index C' satisfies consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C'] > 0 (C' is actively stalling per Rules 56 or 60, meaning its tap window may already be contested): (1) in round R+1, in addition to all Rule 58 actions (corridor ripup + keepout for C + Kelvin force stubs for C), ALSO inject a tier-1 (5mm x 8mm, Rule 56/57 standard first-tier geometry) keepout centered on C''s shunt exit corridor centroid -- the geometric midpoint between C''s shunt inner-edge pad centroids, identical to Rule 56's centroid derivation for C'; (2) do NOT modify consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C'] or kelvin_keepout_escalation_count[C'] for this preemptive injection -- the counters continue advancing normally per Rules 56, 57, and 60 so future escalation is not disrupted; (3) if Rule 56 or 60 would independently inject a keepout for C' in round R+1 (the counter threshold has already been reached), the preemptive injection and the Rule-56/60 injection are merged: use the LARGER of the two geometries (Rule 57 escalated size vs tier-1) and log both triggers; (4) log 'rule58_neighbor_preemptive_corridor_keepout' with fields: (a) round R, (b) cable C (Rule 58 ripup target), (c) list of all C' cables receiving preemptive keepouts with their consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C'] values at time of injection, (d) Rule 58 ripup geometry and each C' keepout geometry injected, (e) whether any C' injection merged with an independently-triggered Rule 56/60 keepout. This rule is additive to Rules 56, 57, 58, 59, and 60; it does not modify post_max_escalation_stall, net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, or any session-scoped state maintained by other rules. Rationale: Rule 59 protects existing Kelvin track segments belonging to C' from being ripped during Rule 58's corridor clearance for C, but does not prevent the newly-rerouted traffic displaced from C's cleared corridor from being PLACED in C''s tap window in round R+1. FR immediately fills the cleared space in the same routing pass, and the closest available corridor space is C''s tap window when it is still open. The three-round lag before Rule 56/60 fires independently for C' (once its stall counter reaches 6) is exactly the window in which competitors re-entrench: rounds 110-112 show /SENSEC2_HI becoming and staying asymmetrically unconnected precisely during Rule 58 activity on cable 1, with cable 2's counter at ~3 of 6. A preemptive tier-1 keepout on C' in the same R+1 round that C's corridor is cleared blocks the entrenchment window without committing to the full escalation ladder for C' prematurely.
